facts.statement: Sachicasaurus is an extinct genus of pliosaurid found in the Barremian of the Paja Formation in the Colombian Eastern Ranges of the Andes.
facts.quote: Sachicasaurus is an extinct genus of brachauchenine pliosaurid known from the Barremian of the Paja Formation, Altiplano Cundiboyacense in the Colombian Eastern Ranges of the Andes.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Sachicasaurus was discovered in 2013.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, MP111209-1, was found in 2013

facts.statement: The type specimen of Sachicasaurus measured approximately 10 to 10.35 meters long and weighed between 10.3 and 12.8 metric tons.
facts.quote: Sachicasaurus was a large pliosaur, with the type specimen measuring approximately 10 - 10.35 m long and weighing 10.3 - 12.8 MT.

facts.statement: Sachicasaurus is characterized by a very short lower jaw symphysis and a reduced number of lower teeth, ranging from 17 to 18 compared to 25 to 40 in other pliosaurids.
facts.quote: Diagnostic features include a very short mandibular symphysis, reduced number of mandibular teeth (17 to 18 versus 25 to 40 in other pliosaurids), slender teeth, among other features.

facts.statement: The preserved length of the holotype is 9.9 meters, suggesting it was a sub-adult individual that may have been missing tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: With a preserved length of 9.9 m (which may be missing the vertebrae from the end of the tail), the specimen is interpreted as a sub-adult individual.

facts.statement: Sachicasaurus is classified as a brachauchenine pliosaurid.
facts.quote: Sachicasaurus is an extinct genus of brachauchenine pliosaurid

facts.statement: Sachicasaurus belongs to the family Pliosauridae.
Sachicasaurus lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, approximately 125.77 to 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Sachicasaurus shared its environment with three other pliosaurids: Acostasaurus, Stenorhynchosaurus, and Monquirasaurus.
facts.quote: Sachicasaurus is one of four pliosaurids from the Paja Formation, others being Acostasaurus, Stenorhynchosaurus, and Monquirasaurus.

facts.statement: Sachicasaurus coexisted with elasmosaurids, marine turtles, and ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaurs in the same region.
facts.quote: Fue contemporáneo además de los elasmosáuridos Callawayasaurus y Leivanectes, la tortuga marina Desmatochelys padillai, la tortuga sandowníida Leyvachelys, y los ictiosaurios oftalmosáuridos Muiscasaurus y Platypterygius sachicarum.

facts.statement: The genus name Sachicasaurus is derived from the location of the fossil find, Sáchica, and the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The genus name Sachicasaurus refers to Sáchica, the location where the fossil was found, and saurus, meaning "lizard" in Latinised Greek.

facts.statement: The species name vitae means "of life" in Latin, chosen to reflect the vitality the discovery brought to the town of Sáchica.
facts.quote: The species epithet vitae, meaning "of life" in Latin, was chosen because of the life in Sáchica the fossil find has sparked.
